Subjective:
- Current issues:
  - 26-year-old female presents with 3-day history of worsening headache.
  - Location: diffuse, with prominence around right eye.
  - Character: dull baseline with intermittent sharper pains; gradual onset at work.
  - Timing: constant with fluctuations in intensity; rated 8/10.
  - Associated symptoms: photophobia; “shooting lights” at onset; nausea without vomiting; difficulty focusing.
  - Denies: loss of vision or blurry vision; speech difficulty; limb weakness; fever; rash; recent head injury.
  - Neck stiffness: initially affirmed then denied (conflict noted).
- Past medical history:
  - No chronic conditions reported.
  - No prior diagnosed migraines; family history positive for migraines in mother and sister.
  - No prior eye exam in many years; wears glasses since childhood.
- Medications:
  - No regular medications.
  - Ibuprofen taken for the last 2 days, 3 tablets/day, minimal relief (dose/route/frequency beyond tablet count not documented).
- Social history:
  - Lives with 3 housemates.
  - Works in IT with heavy computer use; reduced screen brightness due to symptoms.
  - Social smoker; drinks alcohol socially.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies (NKDA).

Objective:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Physical exam: not documented.
- Investigations: none performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute headache with photophobia and visual symptoms
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Likely migraine-type headache.
   - Investigations planned: None today; keep a headache diary to identify potential triggers.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Optimize ibuprofen: up to 2 tablets three times daily (tablet strength not documented).
     - Stronger analgesia discussed: naproxen; may add acetaminophen (paracetamol) or codeine — dose/route/frequency not documented; prescription offered, exact medication not confirmed.
     - Consider repeat eye examination if ongoing eye strain.
     - Safety net: seek care sooner for worsening headache, new vision problems, limb weakness, or general deterioration.
   - Follow-up: 1–2 weeks to reassess; discuss prophylactic therapy if headaches become frequent.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals; focused neurologic exam (cranial nerves, motor/sensory, coordination, gait) and fundoscopic exam.
  - Exact doses/route/frequency for any prescribed/over-the-counter analgesics.
  - Contraceptive use/pregnancy status (clinician asked about oral contraceptive pill; response not documented).
  - Up-to-date eye exam status noted but no formal referral or plan documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Neck stiffness: patient said “Yeah” then “No” (conflict noted).
  - Unclear whether a prescription (and which medication) was actually issued.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; some pauses/false starts; content adequate for clinical documentation.
